When indexing a plain object/record with a key derived from external or user-controlled input (e.g., a file name, extension, or path segment), never use plain bracket access like `table[key]`. Such access silently falls through to inherited `Object.prototype` members (`constructor`, `__proto__`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, etc.), returning unexpected values instead of `undefined` for unknown keys. This can lead to incorrect behavior or exploitable logic depending on how the returned value is used.

Always verify the key is an own property before reading it, or use a `Map` instead of a plain object so prototype chain lookups are impossible:

```ts
function lookup(table: Record<string, IconSpec>, key: string): IconSpec | undefined {
  return Object.hasOwn(table, key) ? table[key] : undefined;
}
```

or, preferably when the mapping is purely data-driven:

```ts
const BY_EXTENSION = new Map<string, IconSpec>([
  ["ts", { icon: CODE, className: "text-sky-600" }],
  // ...
]);
```

Apply this pattern to every lookup table keyed by untrusted strings (file extensions, file names, folder names, language identifiers, etc.), and add regression tests asserting that keys like `"constructor"`, `"__proto__"`, and `"toString"` resolve to the default/fallback value rather than an inherited object.</description>
